claim_verdicts.evidence: Definition of the vocab term, from outline item 1 and misconception 3; no pinned-version document governs it. Round 2: the added sentence on 'service' (s3) matches the claim text.

RFC 9110 9.2.2: "if a client sends a PUT request and the underlying connection is closed before any response is received, then the client can establish a new connection and retry the idempotent request. It knows that repeating the request will have the same intended effect, even if the original request succeeded"; "A client SHOULD NOT automatically retry a request with a non-idempotent method unless it has ... some means to detect that the original request was never applied." A caller without a response cannot know whether the work was done.

"By default, if the database provider supports transactions, all changes in a single call to `SaveChanges` are applied in a transaction. If any of the changes fail, then the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes are applied to the database. This means that `SaveChanges` is guaranteed to either completely succeed, or leave the database unmodified if an error occurs."

Claim text now equals the round-1 suggested_text. BEGIN: "all statements after a BEGIN command will be executed in a single transaction until an explicit COMMIT or ROLLBACK". PREPARE TRANSACTION exists "to allow an external transaction manager to perform atomic global transactions across multiple databases"; the claim and s4/s6/q2 now carry that condition ("Unless something outside both processes coordinates them").

EF Core: "EF Core will treat the supplied SQL as a subquery" when composing (Include). PostgreSQL SELECT: "If a locking clause is applied to a view or sub-query, it affects all tables used in the view or sub-query"; "When a locking clause appears in a sub-SELECT, the rows locked are those returned to the outer query by the sub-query." The sub-query reads notifications only, so joined orders/customers are not locked. Docs opened round 2: sql-select.html, sql-queries.md, C# compiler-messages.

issues.text: New in round 2. "Unless something outside both processes coordinates them" names an exception I cannot picture: nothing I know coordinates two processes' saves. I wondered whether that something would make the second tie unnecessary. Not blocking: the main idea and q2 still work without it, and Connections points to the fix.
issues.quote: Unless something outside both processes coordinates them, placing an order becomes two separate saves, and one can fail alone.
issues.fix: Add a few words after "coordinates them" saying this lesson does not use such coordination and the second tie is still cut, e.g. "(this lesson does not rely on that)"; or drop the clause from section 4 and section 6 if the claim allows.

issues.text: New in round 2. I had to re-read this sentence twice: "adds when to cut" reads oddly, and "where they show up as calls and queries crossing it" stacks three ideas (before the split, boundary inside one process, ties visible as crossings) in one clause.
issues.quote: This lesson adds when to cut the ties: before the split, with the module boundary drawn inside one process, where they show up as calls and queries crossing it.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: "Cut the ties before the split, while the module boundary is still inside one process. There each tie shows up as a call or a query that crosses the boundary."
